ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In order to study the effect of temperature on the activity of a certain enzyme, three experimental groups are set up: group A (20℃), group B (40℃), and group C (60℃). The product concentration of each group at different reaction times is measured (other conditions are the same), and the results are shown in the figure. Answer the question: If at time t2, twice the amount of substrate is added to the reaction system of group C, with other conditions kept unchanged, then at t3, by how many times will the total amount of product in group C increase?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the horizontal axis is reaction time, and the vertical axis is product concentration; the three curves respectively indicate the changes in product concentration over time under conditions of 20℃, 40℃, and 60℃. Group C corresponds to the dashed curve at 60℃; this curve basically becomes a horizontal line after an earlier time, and between t2 and t3 the product concentration does not continue to rise. Reasoning: Group C, at 60℃, has already been in the plateau phase by t2, indicating that the limiting factor at this time is not insufficient substrate, but that high temperature has reduced enzyme activity or even inactivated it, so it cannot continue to catalyze the reaction. Therefore, even if a 2-fold amount of substrate is added at t2, with other conditions unchanged, no more product will be generated by t3.
